issues.description: Enter handling branch bypasses arrow keys, escape, and other navigation keys
issues.detail: The new early-return block runs when the key is anything other than Tab, but it is reached only inside the existing select/enter handling path. If placed incorrectly it could route Up/Down/Escape to textedit. Verify it sits under the Return/Enter branch only — as written here it appears to apply broadly and could break completion navigation.

issues.description: Re-dispatching event to textedit may cause double-processing or recursion
issues.detail: Calling self.textedit.keyPressEvent(event) after self.hide() forwards the original event. Depending on Qt event filter wiring, this can cause the same key to be processed twice (once by the popup, once by the editor) or trigger focus/signal loops. A safer pattern is event.ignore() or posting a synthesized event.
Use `key != Qt.Key_Tab` for readability. Also consider Qt.Key_Backtab for Shift+Tab semantics if relevant. Minor style/clarity nit.

issues.description: No migration/default handling note for existing user configs
issues.detail: The new key `use_enter_for_completions` defaults to True in config/main.py, which preserves current behavior — good. However, there is no CONF_VERSION bump or migration note; existing user config files without the key will fall back to the default via get_conf, which should be verified for the completions section.

issues.description: Missing tooltip/label clarity about which keys still accept
issues.detail: Tooltip says "completions will be accepted with the Tab key only." If the popup also supports double-click or other accept paths, the wording is misleading. Consider "with Tab or mouse click" for accuracy.

issues.description: No test added for the new behavior toggle
issues.detail: Spyder has tests for completion key handling; a small unit/integration test confirming Enter dismisses the popup and forwards to editor when the option is False would prevent regressions when the keyPressEvent logic is later refactored.

review.summary: The PR adds a useful preference to disable Enter accepting completions, with sensible default (True) preserving prior behavior. Main concerns are around the keyPressEvent change: the early-return branch may be reached on non-Enter keys depending on its placement, and re-dispatching the event to textedit risks double-processing. Tooltip wording and minor style nits should be tightened, and a regression test for the new code path would be valuable.
